seed: Objects of type `reflection` under action ACTION4 with touching neighbours [player,wall,wall] show mixed outcomes: h,pixels,y x1, h,pixels,w,x,y x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a global object such as a counter, HUD element or legend, read as state. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Two-axis mirror game on a 21x21 grid of 3x3 blocks. H axis = the wall row (A1 up / A2 down), V axis = the wall column (A3 left / A4 right). A5 cycles the selection H -> V -> pieces (row-major) -> H, and the selected item shows 0 centres.
Pieces (ring 5) move in 4 directions. The board edge and other pieces block them; a blocked move changes no cells, including the HUD.
Each piece block not on an axis is mirrored across H, across V, and across both, drawn as visible solid 4. Piece-covered destinations are skipped and mirrors are clipped to the board.
Draw order is piece > reflection > target 11 > wall, but a target centre 11 shows through every hole and through the selected piece's 0 (this was the one fix after 31/44). HUD column 63 adds one 12 tick per effective action.
The rule is stateless. The suggested global-counter condition for mixed reflection outcomes under A4 was not supported: those outcomes are re-extraction of the redrawn mirrors, and the counter does not gate anything.
